topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the topic of complement and frames its significance and complexity within immunology.

topics.label: Foundations and core mechanics of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the overall purpose, naming conventions, and central C3 activation hub of the complement cascade.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three upstream pathways that detect pathogens and drive surface convertase formation to reach the activation threshold.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the downstream immune outcomes mediated by complement activation, including opsonization, inflammation, and target lysis.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and inhibitory mechanisms that protect host cells from unintended complement destruction.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the distinct disease presentations and clinical phenotypes resulting from specific complement component deficiencies.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how pathogens evade complement-mediated clearance, highlighting the diverse molecular strategies of Staphylococcus aureus.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session on complement and previews the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
